mutants.rationale: Claim every structure satisfying A5 is a well-formed complex; a face with none of its boundary edges present satisfies d1 o d0 = 0 vacuously.
Claim the evaluation-relation axiom can fail on a structure; the reflexive-transitive closure is always a preorder containing the relation.
Claim the non-identification axiom cannot be violated on a one-point carrier; the single pair (0,0) violates it.
Claim a model of all the axioms admits a diagonal pair; A1 excludes it.
Claim the transcribed R_cl rule refuses on a filled triangle; there d1 o d0 = 0, so the exact-but-not-closed cell is empty.
Present A2 (unentailed admission) as a decidable property of finite structures; it is a statement about the status of the admission, not a predicate.
Claim A5 can be violated on a two-point carrier; a face needs three distinct vertices, so A5 is independent only from n = 3.
Count A7 (descent to the quotient) as an independent axiom; it is equivalent to d1 o d0 = 0 on every structure.
Claim the kernel refuses an admission without a token; admit_difference stores the token and never inspects it.
Claim a repeated ordered pair is refused; the kernel appends it again.
Claim admitting (a,b) forbids (b,a); the kernel enforces only a != b and carrier membership.
Swap the order of the two guards: an identical pair outside the carrier raises the A1 error first.
Claim the other axioms force every off-diagonal pair into the admitted set; the models with and without each pair are equinumerous.
Claim R_cl is defined for a half-attached face; there exact cochains with nonzero coboundary exist and R_cl refuses.
Claim a filled triangle has closed non-exact cochains; with the face attached closed means exact there.
Claim the quotient defect is not gauge invariant; shifting by d0(psi) leaves the L1 distance unchanged.
Quote the number of preorders on four points (355) for three points (29).
